# Scaleway Serverless Containers deployment (generated by Cloudhopper)

The Terraform in this directory runs the application as one Scaleway Serverless Container:

- `container.tf`: the container namespace and the container,
- `<function>_schedule_cronTrigger.tf`: a cron trigger per `@ScheduledTrigger` function that calls
  `POST /schedules/<function>`,
- `<function>_event_queueTrigger.tf`: per `@EventTrigger(source = QUEUE)` function a Scaleway Queue
  (SQS), a dead-letter queue `<queue>-dlq` and a trigger that delivers to `POST /events/<function>`,
- `sqs.tf`: activates Scaleway Queues in the project and creates the queue credentials.

Scaleway has no trigger for object storage events; deliver them to `POST /events/<function>` yourself.

Build the image for linux/amd64 from the generated Dockerfile, push it, and apply:

```bash
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t rg.fr-par.scw.cloud/<namespace>/<app>:<version> \
  -f target/deployment/scaleway-terraform/shared-resources_dockerfile..dockerfile .
docker push rg.fr-par.scw.cloud/<namespace>/<app>:<version>
cd target/deployment/scaleway-terraform
cp main.tf.disabled main.tf      # provider configuration; adjust it first
terraform init
terraform apply -var image=rg.fr-par.scw.cloud/<namespace>/<app>:<version>
```

`terraform output url` prints the base URL. See the variables in `container.tf` for scaling,
memory, environment variables and the queue settings. A failing queue message is delivered up to
4 times per receive; after `queue_max_receive_count` receives (default 1) it moves to the
dead-letter queue.
